tasks.short: Set up and operate editing and effects systems

steps.what: Confirm the final product's format, title, effects and delivery requirements
inputs: existing producer-approved brief and delivery specification

steps.what: Set up computer editing, titling, switching and effects project settings
inputs: existing approved project presets and source media metadata

steps.what: Operate the editing, electronic titling, switching and digital effects systems to produce the required sequence
inputs: existing project media and confirmed editing requirements

steps.what: Review the completed product for title, effects, picture and sound errors
outputs: checked final product and resolved defects

steps.what: Approve the exact final product version and export settings
inputs: checked final product and resolved defects
outputs: approved final version and export settings

steps.what: Export the approved final version to the specified internal project destination
inputs: approved final version and export settings

tasks.design: Configure reusable project presets in {OTHER}, the nonlinear editing, titling, switching and effects environment. The editor operates the project, reviews the final product and separately exports the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project settings must fit the actual media and delivery specification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presets can apply verified settings without repeatedly entering them.
tasks.still_hard: Choose and operate effects that serve the intended product.

ambition.what: Support existing project setup without automating creative choices.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0-2; verify media permissions and consultation needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: editing environments support project presets and export settings that an editor can verify.

assumptions: OTHER means the editing/titling/switching/effects software and hardware. Producer supplies the existing delivery specification; media metadata supplies source frame rate, resolution and audio layout. s1 verifies actual requirements, and s2 retains unsupported settings and exceptions. No new upstream metadata capture is assumed free.

Native presets come first. Central applies only where repeated manual setup remains and retains 60% of s2; creative operation, full review and final approval remain unchanged. If presets already cover setup, no change is made and saving is zero.

Export runtime is already automated and excluded from human labour. s6 represents only the near-zero same-system export action and earns no saving. It is not a client send or publication. s5 follows the finished reviewed version; edits invalidate approval.
Provisional B=100, R=92, gross=8; incremental focal preset upkeep=1; net=7. Shares are illustrative and independent of means priors.
unknowns: Current preset coverage and actual manual setup effort.
research_questions: Observe project setup separately from creative operation and export runtime.

already_counted.description: Retained setup checks and exceptions at s2

incremental.description: Maintain approved project presets after specification changes

approvals.approved_version: exact final product version, export settings and internal destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero with existing preset coverage; high allows three additional hours handling unusual media or delivery settings beyond central net 7.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the story brief and specified film segment lengths
inputs: existing producer-approved story brief and duration constraints

steps.what: Watch candidate film segments and assess their contribution to the story
outputs: selected story material and observed limitations

steps.what: Set and record selected segment in/out points and intended sequence order
inputs: selected story material and observed limitations
outputs: confirmed segment ranges and sequence order

steps.what: Trim the specified ranges and reassemble them into the initial sequence
inputs: confirmed segment ranges and sequence order

steps.what: Shape pacing, transitions and segment choices for maximum story effect
Watch and approve the final story sequence and durations
Save the approved final story sequence in the same editing project

tasks.design: Use native range-based sequence assembly in {OTHER}, the nonlinear editor, after the editor selects and records exact segment ranges. Keep story choices, pacing and final viewing with the editor; no model is needed to execute a known cut list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical trimming can only follow exact editorial selections.
tasks.enabler_now: Native sequence tools can apply known frame ranges and order deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Choose segments and timing that communicate the intended story.
tasks.human_edge: Feel pacing and recognise a technically correct but ineffective sequence.

ambition.what: Reduce only supported mechanical assembly effort.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: nonlinear editors can assemble sequences from selected source ranges and order.

assumptions: Boundary includes viewing, selecting, recording edit decisions, assembly, shaping and saving. Producer supplies story/duration requirements; editor produces source clip ID, frame-rate/timebase, in/out frame and order in s3. That decision capture remains fully counted. Invalid ranges or missing media require manual handling.

Native selected-range assembly comes first. Central applies only where manual repeated range placement remains: s4 retains 50% for applying/checking assembly and exceptions. Existing ripple arithmetic, playback and rendering runtime earn no saving; where native assembly is already used, no change is made.

s5 creative shaping and s6 final viewing remain unchanged. Complete sequence exists before approval; edits void approval. Same-system save is approximately zero time and earns no saving. No client send or publication occurs in this boundary.
Provisional B=100, R=90, gross=10; incremental focal preset/range-interface upkeep=1; net=9. Shares are illustrative and independent of means priors.
unknowns: Whether manual assembly remains after existing editor shortcuts and presets.
research_questions: Time selected-range assembly separately from watching, selecting and shaping story segments.

already_counted.description: Retained assembly checks and exceptions at s4

incremental.description: Inspect range and sequence preset failures

approvals.approved_version: complete final story sequence and durations

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero with existing native assembly; high allows three extra hours resolving range/timebase exceptions beyond central net 9.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Cut between shot angles with fluid timing

steps.what: Review the scene and existing synchronised camera angles for usable shot choices
inputs: existing synchronised multicamera footage and camera-track mapping
outputs: reviewed scene coverage and usable angle constraints

steps.what: Make the preliminary cuts between scene angles at candidate speaker changes
inputs: reviewed scene coverage and usable angle constraints
existing synchronised picture and audio tracks

loop.input: synchronised footage, camera mapping and editor-confirmed usable angles
loop.output: draft angle-cut timeline with uncertain speaker or coverage points marked
loop.check: Editor watches cuts for correct speaker/angle, reaction context, continuity and timing; the proposal cannot determine the final story
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction, then manual angle cutting
loop.why_not_simpler: Known edit lists should be applied deterministically; here candidate cut points depend on interpreting speech and visual coverage, so native assisted switching is tested first

steps.what: Refine each angle cut for fluid action, reaction timing and scene continuity
inputs: reviewed scene coverage and usable angle constraints

steps.what: Watch and approve the final scene's individual cuts and overall flow
Save the approved angle-cut sequence in the same editing project

tasks.design: Test native assisted multicamera switching in {OTHER}, the nonlinear editing environment, for a preliminary speaker-led timeline. The editor checks proposed changes, refines every cut and approves the completed scene before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Speaker changes alone do not establish the best visual cut.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded assisted switching can propose a first timeline from synchronised coverage.
tasks.still_hard: Choose reaction shots and time cuts to preserve continuity and dramatic intent.
tasks.human_edge: Judge when a technically plausible switch weakens the scene.

ambition.what: Support preliminary cuts without replacing editorial timing.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3; verify footage processing access and consultation needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: assisted multicamera editing can propose speaker-led shot changes for editor review.

assumptions: Central scenario is synchronised multicamera dialogue, not every scene type. Existing project preparation supplies clip IDs, aligned timecodes, audio tracks and camera mapping; s1 checks mapping and usable angles. Missing synchronisation or ambiguous coverage falls back to manual cuts; no new upstream preparation is free.

Native assisted switching comes first; custom code or an autonomous editor is unnecessary. Central retains 60% of preliminary cutting for proposal review/correction plus all creative refinement and final viewing. Non-dialogue scenes or an existing accepted assisted timeline imply zero additional saving.

Only draft timeline edits occur before final approval. s4 follows the completed scene; changes void approval. Same-system save is approximately zero time and earns no saving. Existing media analysis/render runtime is not focal human work.
Provisional B=100, R=90, gross=10; incremental focal camera/preset exception upkeep=1; net=9. Shares are illustrative and independent of means priors.
unknowns: Share of suitable multicamera scenes and actual proposal correction time.
research_questions: Compare preliminary cutting plus all correction and viewing on representative synchronised dialogue scenes.

already_counted.description: Proposal checking and correction retained in s2

incremental.description: Inspect camera mapping and assisted-switching preset failures

approvals.approved_version: complete refined and reviewed angle-cut sequence

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero for unsuitable or already-assisted scenes; high allows three extra hours correcting speaker/angle proposals beyond central net 9.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review edited films and identify necessary corrections

steps.what: Read the review brief and confirm the exact assembled film version and delivery limits
inputs: producer review brief and technical delivery specification

steps.what: Check the edited film for technical signal defects and inspect flagged locations
inputs: existing film picture/audio data and approved technical thresholds
outputs: verified technical defects and dismissed flags

steps.what: Watch the assembled film on a monitor to judge story, continuity, performance and pacing corrections
Record actual required corrections with timecodes and reasons
inputs: verified technical defects and dismissed flags

steps.what: Check and approve the final correction list against the reviewed film version
Save the approved correction list in the same project review record

tasks.design: Configure native technical quality checks in {OTHER}, the editing and review environment, against approved signal thresholds. Keep full editorial viewing, actual correction-note capture and final correction decisions with the editor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical flags cannot determine whether a scene works editorially.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic signal checks can direct attention to potential black frames, clipping or specification mismatches.
tasks.still_hard: Decide whether a flagged feature is intentional and whether the story needs correction.
tasks.human_edge: Judge meaning, continuity and pacing across the whole film.

ambition.what: Support the current review with technical flags only.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0-2; verify media access and review permissions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: editing and quality-control tools can flag signal-threshold violations for a person to inspect.

assumptions: Producer supplies actual reviewed version ID and delivery specification; existing technical owner supplies allowed thresholds. s1 verifies them. Native checks read actual media samples; s2 includes inspecting flags and manually handling unsupported checks. No model infers editorial defects from signal values.

Central applies only where a distinct manual technical-check pass remains today: s2 retains 60%, while s3 full editorial viewing is unchanged. If native technical checks already run, their runtime is already automated and earns no saving; no change is made for that work.

s4 explicitly captures actual timecode, defect, reason and proposed correction from the editor's decisions. Native marker/report forms are considered; no separate copying baseline or note-writing saving is assumed. Implementing corrections and client sends are outside this review statement.

s5 follows the completed list and binds its review version; changes void approval. Same-system save is approximately zero time and earns no saving. Provisional B=100, R=92, gross=8; incremental focal threshold/false-flag upkeep=1; net=7. Shares are illustrative and independent of means priors.
unknowns: Current technical-check coverage and actual false-flag handling time.
research_questions: Time the distinct technical-check pass and verify all flags while retaining full editorial viewing.

already_counted.description: Flag inspection and manual technical exceptions retained in s2

incremental.description: Review thresholds and recurring false flags

approvals.approved_version: complete final timecoded correction list bound to the reviewed film version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero with existing native checks or no distinct technical pass; high allows three extra hours handling false technical flags beyond central net 7.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Editors retain story, timing and final viewing; native presets, mechanical assembly and bounded proposals support specific operations.
reach: Media technical operator: learn delivery thresholds and source timebases
skills_to_grow: Separate mechanical execution from editorial decisions
Check assisted angle cuts in context
Verify final versions and actual correction timecodes
role.ambitious_version: An editor uses supported tools to reach a first sequence while preserving deliberate story choices and complete final review.
